backup.label: Backup & IRE
backup.title: Backup and IRE
backup.facilitator_intro: Start with backup architecture and scope to establish what GIC believes is protected, then layer through immutability, isolation, and retention governance before probing access controls, detection, and integrity validation. Use the sub-questions to push past polished answers and surface what has actually been operationally proven — not what is documented in policy or assumed by design.

layers.title: Architecture, Scope & Immutability Foundation
layers.intent: Establish what backup infrastructure exists and what immutability model underpins it before probing whether controls are enforced.

questions.primary: Paint a picture of the backup architecture — what platforms and architectures protect GIC's critical systems today, and which systems, data sets, and service tiers are included in enterprise backup scope?
sub_questions: Which backup platform protects which workload class — block, file, object, SaaS, database, container?
Are multiple backup platforms in play, and where do their boundaries overlap or leave gaps?
What percentage of in-scope systems are reporting successful backups in the last 7 days?
Which workloads are explicitly out of scope, and on what rationale?
Are SaaS workloads such as M365, Salesforce, and Workday covered by an enterprise backup tool, or assumed to be vendor-protected?

questions.primary: What immutability controls are implemented across backup repositories and tiers — what mode is used for each tier, and what drove those design decisions?
sub_questions: Which tier uses compliance lock (truly unbreakable) versus governance lock (admin-removable)?
How does immutability differ between primary, secondary, and air-gapped or vault tiers?
Is immutability applied at job-creation, post-write, or via policy inheritance?
Can immutability be silently bypassed via API, service account, or vendor support backdoor?
When was the immutability design last reviewed against current ransomware TTPs?

layers.title: Isolation, Retention & Encryption Governance
layers.intent: Move from 'what is immutable' to 'how is it isolated, governed, and protected' — this is where design intent and operational reality commonly diverge.

questions.primary: How are backup copies isolated from production systems and administrative domains — is air-gapping logical, physical, scheduled, one-way, or vendor-purpose-built — and which backup copies are considered the recovery source of last resort for crown-jewel services?
sub_questions: What network path exists between production AD or Entra and the backup admin plane?
Is the air-gap one-way (production to vault) or bidirectional? What triggers the gap to close — schedule, event, or manual action?
Which exact copy is the recovery source of last resort, where is it, and who knows it exists?
Has anyone ever actually restored from the last-resort copy — in a test or in anger?
If the primary backup environment were compromised, how long until the last-resort copy could be brought online?

questions.primary: How are retention lock periods determined and governed — who can extend, shorten, or remove retention locks, what approval model is enforced — and how are legal hold and preservation requirements integrated into backup immutability controls?
sub_questions: Walk us through the approval flow if someone wanted to shorten a 7-year retention lock today — who signs, who approves?
Can a single admin act alone, or is dual-authorization or 4-eyes enforced for lock changes?
Are retention lock changes logged immutably, and who actively reviews those logs?
How are legal hold requests received, validated, and applied to backup catalogs?
What happens when legal hold conflicts with a retention reduction request?

questions.primary: Are immutable backup copies encrypted, and where are the keys held — and what happens if encryption keys, KMS, HSM, or identity dependencies are unavailable during recovery?
sub_questions: Where is the KMS or HSM physically and logically hosted — on-prem, cloud, vendor-managed?
If production AD is unavailable, can backup admins still authenticate to KMS to unlock encrypted backups?
Are escrow copies of keys held, and who controls escrow access?
Has a "no KMS, no identity, restore anyway" scenario ever been walked through end-to-end?
What is the documented bootstrap order if both identity and KMS are unavailable?

layers.title: Access Controls, Detection & Integrity Validation
layers.intent: Probe who can touch backup infrastructure, whether tampering would be detected, and whether backups are trusted before restoration.

questions.primary: Is MFA enforced for backup administrative access, and is the admin identity store separated from production identity — and are break-glass backup recovery accounts defined, protected, and periodically validated?
sub_questions: Is backup admin identity in the same forest or Entra tenant as production users, or genuinely separated?
If production AD is encrypted, can backup admins still log in to initiate recovery?
How are break-glass credentials stored, rotated, and access-tested?
When was the last validated use of a break-glass account?
Are break-glass actions automatically alerted to SOC and security leadership, and reviewed afterward?

questions.primary: Is PAM used to broker privileged access to backup platforms or cyber recovery storage — and how are vendor or third-party support paths into the backup environment controlled and monitored?
sub_questions: Are backup admin sessions brokered through PAM, or do admins log in directly with cached credentials?
Are session recordings retained for all backup admin activity, and reviewed for high-risk actions?
How do vendor support engineers (Rubrik, Cohesity, Veeam, Dell, Commvault) actually access the environment?
Is vendor access time-bound, per-session approved, and fully logged?
What happens if the PAM platform itself is unavailable during a recovery scenario?

questions.primary: How are backup infrastructure logs monitored for tampering, retention changes, deletion attempts, or anomalous behaviour — and how quickly can malicious backup tampering or immutability changes be detected?
sub_questions: Where are backup platform logs forwarded — enterprise SIEM, isolated cyber-recovery SOC, or only locally retained?
What specific alerts fire for retention lock changes, immutability disables, mass deletes, or anomalous restore activity?
What is the documented MTTD for backup tampering, and has it been measured rather than modelled?
Are backup admin actions correlated with identity-side anomalies (privileged logons, new accounts, AD changes)?
Are canary backups or honeypot artifacts deployed to detect intruder reconnaissance?

questions.primary: Are backups scanned for malware or pre-existing compromise before being trusted for restoration — is there an isolated recovery environment or clean room for validating crown-jewel recoveries before production reintroduction — and how are integrity checks performed on immutable or air-gapped backup copies?
sub_questions: Which scanning engine runs against backups, on what cadence, and at what depth — signature, behavioural, ML?
What happens when a backup is flagged — quarantined, alerted, or simply noted in a report?
What does the clean room actually look like — isolated VLAN, separate vCenter, dedicated identity plane?
How is the clean room itself kept clean and rebuilt between recovery cycles?
Are integrity checks (checksum, hash, restore-verification) periodic, or only invoked at restore time?

layers.title: Recovery Readiness & Dependencies
layers.intent: Test whether backup coverage, recovery objectives, and testing practices can actually deliver recovery under pressure.

questions.primary: Are crown-jewel, critical, SaaS, database, container, and unstructured data sources all protected by consistent backup standards — and what are the defined RTO and RPO targets for critical systems, and do current backup architectures realistically support them?
sub_questions: For each major data class, what RTO and RPO are technically achievable today — not promised, but proven?
Where do RTO/RPO commitments to the business diverge from operational reality?
Have RTO/RPO targets been validated in tests, or only documented in policy and BIA?
Who owns the gap when an RTO or RPO is missed — IT, business, risk, or no one?

questions.primary: Which systems currently have the largest gap between recovery objectives and actual backup recoverability — and how often are recovery tests performed, validating full business service recovery rather than isolated system restores?
sub_questions: Name the top three systems where recovery would currently miss its RTO under realistic conditions.
Are recovery tests scoped to individual systems, or to full business services such as trade settlement, payments, or reporting?
Are tests scenario-based (ransomware, regional loss, supply chain) or technical-only?
Are tests independent and unannounced, or scheduled with full team preparation?
Who participates in recovery tests — IT only, or business owners, risk, and leadership too?

questions.primary: Have full end-to-end recoveries from immutable or isolated copies been completed within the last 12 months — and what dependencies must survive or be rebuilt before backup restoration can begin successfully?
sub_questions: Of recovery tests in the last 12 months, how many specifically sourced data from immutable or isolated copies?
What is the documented recovery sequence — what services must come back first?
Have those dependencies themselves been recovery-tested, or only assumed?
Which dependencies (DNS, identity, KMS, vCenter, networking, ticketing, monitoring) must be live before restore can even begin?
Has a "cold start" — every dependency down, recover from scratch — ever been walked through?

questions.primary: How are backup platforms, metadata, catalogs, and admin controls protected if core identity services are impaired — and what would a responder actually need to reconnect or rebuild before the first critical restore can begin?
sub_questions: If production AD or Entra is fully encrypted, can backup admins still authenticate to the backup management plane?
Where is the backup catalog and metadata stored, and what is its own recovery posture?
Are backup admin credentials cached locally on appliances, kept in vault-isolated identity, or always dependent on production identity?
What is the documented rebuild plan for the backup management plane itself if it is compromised?

layers.title: Evidence & Priorities
layers.intent: Anchor the conversation in what has actually been proven and where the highest-impact improvements lie.

questions.primary: What evidence best demonstrates that backup can support trusted recovery under cyber-compromise conditions — not just that backups exist, but that they have been validated, restored, and reintroduced cleanly?
sub_questions: Show us the most recent successful cyber-recovery test report — what scenario, scope, and outcomes were documented?
What scenarios have been run against immutable copies in the last 12 months, and what failed?
What is the documented evidence chain from "backup exists" to "data restored" to "service running cleanly"?
Have auditors, regulators, or independent third parties validated recovery claims, or have they been self-attested?

questions.primary: If a cyber-compromise hit today and crown-jewel recovery depended on immutable or isolated copies, what would most likely undermine that recovery — and what backup improvements would most materially strengthen cyber recovery readiness?
sub_questions: If you had to name a single dependency that would break recovery today, what would it be — and why hasn't it been fixed?
Where would Day 2 of a real ransomware recovery hit the wall — identity, DNS, capacity, scanning, clean room, or coordination?
If you had budget and political capital for exactly one backup-domain improvement this year, what would deliver the most cyber-recovery uplift?
What does the 12-month backup and cyber-recovery roadmap actually look like, and how was it prioritised?

granular_questions.question: What immutability controls are implemented on backup platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through your immutability story end-to-end: when a backup is written, what mechanism makes it tamper-proof, and how confident is the team that this would hold up under a determined adversary with admin credentials?

granular_questions.question: Are backups protected from deletion or modification?
granular_questions.discussion: If a senior backup admin's account were compromised tomorrow morning, what would they actually be able to destroy before anyone noticed, and how do you know?

granular_questions.question: What immutability mode is in use per backup tier (compliance/regulatory lock vs governance lock)?
granular_questions.discussion: Talk us through the trade-off you made between operational flexibility and absolute immutability: where did you choose governance lock over compliance lock, and why?

granular_questions.question: Is logical or physical air-gapping used?
granular_questions.discussion: How would you describe the level of isolation between your production environment and your last-line-of-defense backup copy to an auditor, and where would that description start to feel uncomfortable?

granular_questions.question: Is the air-gapped/isolated environment a vendor-purpose-built solution (e.g., Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery, Rubrik Cloud Vault, Cohesity FortKnox, Veeam Hardened Repository, AWS S3 Object Lock with Vault Lock, Azure Immutable Blob, Pure SafeMode, NetApp SnapLock Compliance)?
granular_questions.discussion: What was the rationale for choosing your current air-gap or cyber recovery vault solution, and where do you feel its limits today?

granular_questions.question: How are backup copies isolated from production environments?
granular_questions.discussion: Looking at your backup network architecture, where are the trust boundaries, and which of those boundaries would you most like to harden if budget were not a constraint?

granular_questions.question: Is the air-gap network connection one-way (data diode, scheduled sync) or persistent?
granular_questions.discussion: Is the connection between production and your isolated environment ever active in both directions, and if so, when, why, and for how long?

granular_questions.question: Is the isolated environment under a different administrative domain, identity store, and tooling stack?
granular_questions.discussion: Is the isolated environment truly run as a separate domain (different identity, different tooling, different team), or does it share roots with production in ways that worry you?

granular_questions.question: Are immutable storage features enforced across all backup tiers?
granular_questions.discussion: Across your different backup tiers (primary, secondary, archive, cloud, SaaS), where is immutability strongest and where is it weakest? Are there tiers where it is purely policy-based rather than technically enforced?

granular_questions.question: What is the minimum and maximum retention lock period configured, and how was it derived from BIA RPO/RTO and regulatory requirements (MAS TRM, PDPA)?
granular_questions.discussion: How were the retention lock durations actually derived: was it a BIA output, a regulatory floor, or a vendor default that no one has revisited since deployment?

granular_questions.question: Who has authority to extend, shorten, or remove a retention lock, and is dual-control or quorum approval enforced?
granular_questions.discussion: If a senior leader urgently demanded that retention be reduced for cost or capacity reasons, what would actually have to happen procedurally for that to be executed, and how robust is that process under pressure?

granular_questions.question: Is dual-control or quorum approval enforced?
Is there a cooling-off or delayed-delete window for any retention reduction request?
granular_questions.discussion: Is there a delayed-delete or cooling-off window built in, and if so, what is the rationale for the duration chosen and how was it socialised with the business?

granular_questions.question: How are legal holds and litigation preservation integrated with immutability?
granular_questions.discussion: How are legal hold and immutability reconciled when they conflict, for example, when retention says delete but litigation says preserve?

granular_questions.question: Is MFA enforced for all backup console, repository, and storage admin access?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what MFA looks like for your backup admins on a normal day, and what it looks like during a major incident at 2am. Are those two experiences different?

granular_questions.question: Is the backup admin identity store separated from the production AD/IdP (i.e., would a domain compromise also compromise backup access)?
granular_questions.discussion: If your production Active Directory were compromised tonight, which of your backup systems would still let an authorized admin log in tomorrow morning?

granular_questions.question: Are break-glass accounts defined for backup recovery, and where are credentials stored?
granular_questions.discussion: Where are your break-glass credentials physically stored, who has access, and when was the last time they were rotated and tested?

granular_questions.question: Is PAM (CyberArk or equivalent) used to broker privileged backup admin sessions?
granular_questions.discussion: How are privileged backup sessions brokered today, and what would change operationally if you lost access to PAM during an incident?

granular_questions.question: What dependencies are required to access isolated or immutable backup copies during a crisis?
granular_questions.discussion: Imagine production identity, DNS, and network are all unavailable. Walk us through the first hour of accessing the isolated backup environment: who does what, with what credentials, on what hardware?

granular_questions.question: Are vendor support accounts time-bound, logged, and approved per session?
granular_questions.discussion: How does vendor remote access into the backup environment work, and what controls assure you that a compromise of the vendor would not become a compromise of your backups?

granular_questions.question: Are immutable backups encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys, and where are those keys held (HSM, KMS, separate from the backup platform)?
granular_questions.discussion: Where do the keys protecting your immutable backups actually live, and is there any scenario where loss of key custody would render the immutable data unrecoverable?

granular_questions.question: If keys are lost, can the immutable data still be recovered (key escrow / recovery procedure)?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what happens to your immutable data if the key custodians become unavailable: vacation, departure, or worse.

granular_questions.question: Are keys rotated, and does rotation invalidate older immutable copies?
granular_questions.discussion: How does key rotation interact with long-retention immutable data: does rotation create operational drag or recovery risk over time?

granular_questions.question: For cloud-stored immutable copies, is the cloud provider's root/owner account isolated with MFA and is account closure protected?
granular_questions.discussion: Who actually owns the cloud root or top-level account that hosts your immutable cloud copies, and how is that account protected from both insiders and external compromise?

granular_questions.question: How does the platform protect against ransomware targeting backups?
granular_questions.discussion: What ransomware scenarios have you stress-tested the backup platform against, and which attacker techniques (admin compromise, hypervisor escape, retention manipulation) are you most concerned about today?

granular_questions.question: Can backup data be altered by administrators?
granular_questions.discussion: If you were the malicious insider trying to quietly weaken the recovery posture without triggering alerts, what would you target, and would your detection controls catch you?

granular_questions.question: Are there monitoring controls for tampering attempts?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the last time a backup-related alert fired in SIEM: what was the response, the time to triage, and was it tied to a documented use case?

granular_questions.question: How is immutability validated periodically to ensure controls are functioning as intended?
granular_questions.discussion: When was the last time someone actively tried to delete or modify an immutable backup as part of a test, and what did the team learn from that exercise?

granular_questions.question: Are backup infrastructure logs forwarded to SIEM, with use cases for mass deletion attempts, retention reductions, immutability disablement, and anomalous data change rates?
granular_questions.discussion: What backup-related SIEM use cases are live today, and what would you most like to add if the SOC had bandwidth?

granular_questions.question: Is there behavioral/anomaly detection on backup data (entropy spikes suggesting encryption-in-flight)?
granular_questions.discussion: If ransomware encryption activity began silently in production this afternoon, would your backup platform see the anomaly before or after the SOC, and how?

granular_questions.question: Are audit logs themselves stored on immutable/WORM media separate from the backup platform?
granular_questions.discussion: If an attacker compromised the backup admin and tried to cover their tracks in audit logs, where would they fail, and where might they succeed?

granular_questions.question: How long does it take to detect a malicious deletion or retention-modification attempt — what is the documented MTTD?
granular_questions.discussion: What is your honest expectation of how long a malicious deletion attempt would go undetected, and what investments would shorten that window most?

granular_questions.question: Which backup copies are considered the recovery source of last resort for crown-jewel systems?
granular_questions.discussion: If everything else is gone (production, secondary, replicas), which copy do you recover from, where is it, and how confident are you that it is intact today, not last quarter?

granular_questions.question: Are backups scanned for malware and pre-existing implants before being marked as a trusted recovery source?
granular_questions.discussion: How do you assure yourselves that what you are about to restore is not already infected, and what is your process if scanning flags something?

granular_questions.question: Is there an Isolated Recovery Environment (IRE) or clean room where crown-jewel recoveries Is there an Isolated Recovery Environment (IRE) / clean room for validating crown‑jewel recoveries?
granular_questions.discussion: Do you have a true clean-room recovery environment, and if not, what would it take operationally and financially to stand one up?

granular_questions.question: Are integrity checks (hash, checksum, CRC) performed on immutable copies on a defined schedule, and what is the drift remediation process?
granular_questions.discussion: How would you discover bit-rot or silent corruption on a five-year-old immutable copy before you needed to restore from it?

granular_questions.question: Has a full recovery from the air-gapped copy been performed end-to-end in the last 12 months, with documented RTO achieved?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the last full end-to-end recovery test from the isolated environment: what surprised the team, and what did not get retested afterward?

granular_questions.question: Are crown-jewel / CII / MAS-critical systems explicitly mapped to which immutable tier protects them (asset-to-protection traceability)?
granular_questions.discussion: If we asked a business owner of a tier-1 application where their backup is and how to recover it, would their answer match what your team would say?

granular_questions.question: Are SaaS data sources (M365, Salesforce, Workday, etc.) covered by immutable backup, or relying solely on vendor-native retention?
granular_questions.discussion: How are you treating M365, Salesforce, Workday, and similar SaaS data: is the vendor's native retention enough, or have you brought it under your own immutability regime?

granular_questions.question: Are databases, Kubernetes/container persistent volumes, and unstructured file shares all covered by the same immutability standard?
granular_questions.discussion: How well do your immutability standards extend to containers, Kubernetes persistent volumes, and DevOps-managed data, and where are the team boundaries that complicate this?

granular_questions.question: Are there any datasets or platforms not currently protected by immutable or isolated backup patterns?
granular_questions.discussion: If we mapped every system in the CMDB against your immutability coverage, where would the most uncomfortable gaps appear, and what is keeping them there (technology, cost, ownership, awareness)?

granular_questions.question: During a destructive incident, what production dependencies (DNS, AD, PKI, KMS, network, jump hosts) must survive or be rebuilt before the immutable copy can be accessed?
granular_questions.discussion: Have you ever drawn the full dependency chain between a destructive incident and accessing your last-line-of-defense backup? Where does the chain feel fragile?

granular_questions.question: Is there an out-of-band runbook (printed/offline) for invoking the air-gapped recovery process when production identity and tooling are unavailable?
granular_questions.discussion: If your wiki, ticketing, and chat were all unavailable, where would your team find the recovery runbook, and is the version they would find current?

granular_questions.question: How does the immutable backup design map to MAS TRM Notice 21 (system recovery) and the MAS Cyber Hygiene Notice?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how the current immutable backup design maps to MAS TRM Notice 21 system recovery expectations, and where you anticipate regulator pushback.

granular_questions.question: For systems classified as CII under the Cybersecurity Act, has the backup design been reviewed against the CSA CCoP v2.0 backup and recovery requirements?
granular_questions.discussion: For systems designated CII under the Cybersecurity Act, where do you feel most confident, and least confident, meeting the CCoP backup and recovery requirements?

granular_questions.question: Is data residency for backup copies (including cloud-stored immutable copies) aligned with PDPA and any GIC data classification policy that restricts cross-border replication?
granular_questions.discussion: Are there immutable copies in geographies that could create PDPA or cross-border data exposure if invoked during an incident?

granular_questions.question: Are control evidence artefacts maintained for ISO 27001:2022 A.8.13 (information backup) and NIST CSF PR.DS-11 / RC.RP?
granular_questions.discussion: If an external assessor asked for evidence of A.8.13, PR.DS-11, or RC.RP control operation tomorrow, what would your team hand over and what would still need to be assembled?

granular_questions.question: What are the defined RTOs for critical systems?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how 'critical' is currently defined at GIC and how that classification translates into specific RTO commitments. Where do business stakeholders, application owners, and the backup team typically agree or push back on these definitions, and how are disagreements ultimately resolved?

granular_questions.question: What are the defined RPOs for critical systems?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the conversations you have had with business owners around acceptable data loss windows. How do you reconcile what the business wants (often near-zero) with what the backup infrastructure can realistically deliver, and what trade-offs have shaped today's RPO commitments?

granular_questions.question: How are RTO/RPO values determined and approved?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through the governance journey of an RTO/RPO value: from initial proposal, through challenge and review, to formal sign-off. Who has the final say, who can veto, and where in this process do the values get genuinely tested versus rubber-stamped?

granular_questions.question: Do backup architectures align with defined RTO/RPO targets?
granular_questions.discussion: Looking across the current backup landscape (storage tiers, replication topology, backup windows, immutability, restore mechanisms), where are design choices clearly aligned with stated objectives, and where do you suspect the architecture is silently under- or over-provisioned relative to commitments made to the business?

granular_questions.question: Are different tiers of systems mapped to different recovery objectives?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how the tiering model has evolved at GIC. Is it driven primarily by technical attributes, business impact, regulatory mandates such as MAS TRM, or a blend? How often do you find systems mis-tiered, and what typically triggers a re-tiering conversation?

granular_questions.question: Are recovery objectives formally documented?
granular_questions.discussion: Where does the authoritative source-of-truth for RTO and RPO live today: CMDB, BIA documents, runbooks, application catalog, or somewhere else? When auditors or regulators ask, how confident are you that the documented values still match operational reality across all in-scope systems?

granular_questions.question: Are gaps between objectives and capabilities identified?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the most recent meaningful gap identified between a stated RTO/RPO and the actual recovery capability. How was it surfaced (a test, an audit, an incident, a vendor change), and how was it ultimately remediated, accepted as residual risk, or deferred?

granular_questions.question: Which systems currently have the largest gap between target and actual recoverability?
granular_questions.discussion: Without naming specific applications, what patterns do you see in where the largest gaps cluster: legacy platforms, vendor-managed systems, third-party SaaS, very large databases, mainframe? What is the recurring root cause, and who owns the path to closing those gaps?

granular_questions.question: Are recovery objectives linked to application dependency chains and service restart order?
granular_questions.discussion: How confident are you in the documented upstream and downstream dependencies for Tier-1 applications? When was restart sequencing last validated through an actual recovery test, and what surprises did that reveal about hidden dependencies, shared services, or integration points?

granular_questions.question: How are recovery objectives updated when architecture, business criticality, or data profiles change?
granular_questions.discussion: How well-integrated is RTO/RPO review into change management, architecture review boards, and new-application onboarding? Where in the lifecycle do recovery objectives most often get overlooked, and how do you catch the systems that quietly drift out of alignment over time?

granular_questions.question: What constraints would most likely prevent achievement of target RTO/RPO during a real event?
granular_questions.discussion: If a major destructive cyber event (ransomware, supply chain compromise, insider attack) hit GIC tomorrow, where do you genuinely believe the recovery effort would slow down: backup integrity verification, infrastructure capacity, decision authority, vendor response, network bandwidth, or people availability? Which of these concerns you the most, and why?

granular_questions.question: Are RTO and RPO objectives validated through periodic recovery testing, and how are test results fed back into the objectives?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what 'recovery testing' looks like at GIC today: frequency, scope, realism of scenarios, and degree of business participation. When tests reveal that an objective is not achievable, how does that finding actually flow back into updating the documented RTO/RPO or into a remediation plan?

granular_questions.question: Are separate or more stringent recovery objectives defined for cyber-incident scenarios (e.g., ransomware, destructive attack) versus traditional infrastructure outages?
granular_questions.discussion: How has the rise of ransomware and destructive attacks changed the way you think about recovery objectives? Have you defined separate cyber-recovery RTO/RPO targets, an isolated recovery environment, or clean-room patterns, and how are the trade-offs between speed of recovery and assurance of clean data being balanced?

granular_questions.question: How do MAS Technology Risk Management (TRM) and other regulatory expectations shape the way RTO/RPO are set, reviewed, and reported?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how MAS TRM, BCM Notice 644 / Technology Risk Notice expectations, and any internal or board-level policies translate into the way RTO/RPO are set, monitored, and reported at GIC. Where do regulatory expectations push the bar higher than what business stakeholders alone would set?

granular_questions.question: How often are recovery tests performed?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the testing cadence today. What drives the schedule, regulatory expectations, internal policy, business pressure, or available test windows? When was the last time the cadence was deliberately reviewed, and what would prompt you to test more often?

granular_questions.question: What types of restore tests are conducted (full, partial, scenario-based)?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the mix of tests you actually run versus what's on paper. Where do partial restores or tabletops stand in for full recoveries, and what's the honest reason behind that choice? Cost, downtime risk, complexity, or something else?

granular_questions.question: Are critical systems included in restore testing scope?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through how 'in scope' is decided for any given test cycle. Are there critical systems that have been deferred year after year, and if so, what's keeping them out? How do you know the scope reflects real business criticality and not just what is easy to test?

granular_questions.question: Do tests validate actual recovery times vs RTO targets?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about a test where measured recovery time landed far from the documented RTO. What did you do with that finding, and how was it communicated back to application owners and senior stakeholders?

granular_questions.question: Do results provide confidence in operational recovery capability?
granular_questions.discussion: If a major incident happened next week, how confident would you personally feel in the recovery? Where does that confidence come from, recent test results, vendor assurances, or experience, and where are the soft spots you would privately flag?

granular_questions.question: Are results documented, reviewed, and remediated?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what happens to a test report once it's written. Who reads it, who challenges it, and what decisions actually get made on the back of it? Where does the report stop short of driving real change?

granular_questions.question: Are failures or delays tracked and remediated?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the last few recovery test failures that left a remediation tail. How long did closure take, and where do issues tend to get stuck, infrastructure, vendor dependency, ownership, or budget?

granular_questions.question: Do tests simulate real-world disruption scenarios?
granular_questions.discussion: How realistic are the scenarios you test against today? Do they reflect the kind of cyber events GIC genuinely worries about (ransomware, destructive insider, regional outage), or do they default to the easier infrastructure failure cases?

granular_questions.question: Do tests validate recovery of complete business services or only individual systems/data sets?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the difference, at GIC, between successfully restoring a database and successfully restoring the business service that depends on it. How often do tests cross that boundary, and what gets exposed when they do?

granular_questions.question: What were the primary failure points or delays in the most recent large-scale recovery test?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what actually went wrong, or slowed things down, in your most recent large-scale test. Were the issues technical, procedural, decision-making, or coordination across teams? What surprised you the most?

granular_questions.question: Are recovery tests conducted under degraded conditions such as identity, network, or storage impairment?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how realistic it is to lose Active Directory, the network backbone, or primary storage during a recovery, and have you ever tested with those assumptions intentionally degraded? If not, what is holding that back?

granular_questions.question: How is “clean recovery” confirmed before restored systems are returned to business use?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how 'clean' is defined and proven before a restored system goes back into production. Who has the authority to declare cleanliness, what evidence do they rely on, and what tension exists between business pressure to resume and security's need for assurance?

granular_questions.question: How are recovery tests integrated with cyber incident response, ransomware playbooks, and tabletop exercises?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how recovery testing connects to cyber incident response and ransomware playbook exercises. Are they run together, sequenced, or completely separate? Where do you see the seams between BAU recovery testing and cyber-led recovery exercises causing confusion in a real event?

granular_questions.question: Are third-party and SaaS-hosted critical applications included in the recovery testing program, and how is provider testing evidence validated?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how you gain assurance over recovery for SaaS and vendor-hosted applications. Do you accept SOC 2 reports and provider attestations, run joint tests, or treat those systems as black boxes? Where does that approach concern you most?

granular_questions.question: What independent validation (internal audit, external assessment, or regulatory inspection) has been performed on the recovery testing program, and what findings remain open?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how internal audit, MAS inspections, and external assessments have shaped the recovery testing program. What findings have stuck, what changed materially as a result, and where do you think the program would still struggle under independent scrutiny today?

granular_questions.question: How are databases backed up (full, incremental, log-based)?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how backup methods differ across your database estate. Where is it native vendor tooling, where is it agent-based, where is snapshot or storage-level, and why? What dictates the choice for any given platform?

granular_questions.question: Is point-in-time recovery (PITR) supported?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us where PITR genuinely works end-to-end at GIC, and where it is nominal but has never been exercised under real corruption or ransomware conditions. Which databases would you confidently roll back five minutes, and which would you not?

granular_questions.question: How frequently are database backups performed?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the cadence of database backups against the RPO promised to the business. Where are the two clearly aligned, and where is there silent drift: log gaps, missed snapshots, replication lag, suppressed alerts?

granular_questions.question: Are database backups integrated into enterprise backup platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through how database backups sit relative to the enterprise backup platform. Which DBAs run their own, which feed the central platform, and where do those approaches conflict on retention, encryption, immutability, or visibility?

granular_questions.question: How are database backups secured and stored?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how database backup data is secured: encryption at rest, key management, immutability, network segmentation from production. Where are the gaps you would not want highlighted in an audit report?

granular_questions.question: Are database transaction logs, archive logs, and backup metadata themselves protected with the same encryption, immutability, and access controls as the backup data they describe?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how transaction logs, archive logs, and backup metadata are protected. Are they on the same storage, same controls, and same admins as the backup data they describe, and how would you know if logs had been tampered with or quietly truncated?

granular_questions.question: Are database restores regularly tested?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what restore testing of databases actually looks like. Frequency, realism, scope across vendor platforms, and most importantly, do tests prove restoration of usable data or just the technical success of the restore job?

granular_questions.question: Can databases be restored to a known good state after incidents?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how confident you are that, after a destructive event, you could restore each tier-1 database to a known good state and prove it. Where does that confidence come from, and what would change your view: more frequent test restores, application-side validation, or something else?

granular_questions.question: What dependencies must be present before critical databases can be restored successfully?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the dependencies that have to line up before a critical database can come back: identity, KMS, network, license servers, replication links, dependent middleware. Has anyone walked that chain recently for the most critical platforms?

granular_questions.question: How is the correct restore point identified after corruption, operational error, or ransomware?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through how you identify the right restore point after a slow-burn corruption or stealthy ransomware. What evidence do you rely on, who decides, and how recently has the team practised picking the right point in time under pressure?

granular_questions.question: What database platforms have the highest restore complexity or longest expected recovery duration?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through which database platforms you genuinely worry about most in a recovery scenario. Mainframe, very large Oracle, distributed NoSQL, SaaS-hosted? Where is restore complexity highest, and where has duration been longest in past tests?

granular_questions.question: Are database restores tested in a way that validates application usability after recovery?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how restore testing involves the application teams. Do they actually log in, run transactions, and reconcile data after a test, or does the test stop at the database service coming up? Where does that boundary cost you confidence in real recovery?

granular_questions.question: How are database-tier RTO and RPO commitments reconciled with the application-tier and business service RTO/RPO that depend on them?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how database-tier RTO and RPO map up to the application service RTO and RPO the business actually sees. Where are they consistent, and where does the database team commit to numbers the application above cannot actually meet?

granular_questions.question: Are tier-1 databases protected with deliberately layered approaches (native vendor tooling plus enterprise backup, primary plus secondary copy, on-prem plus cloud), and how is that redundancy verified rather than assumed?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us where you deliberately have layered protection: native vendor backup plus enterprise platform, primary plus secondary copy, on-prem plus cloud. How is that redundancy verified, and where do you suspect the layers are protecting the same data twice rather than providing real diversity?

granular_questions.question: Who has administrative access to backup platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through the current population of backup administrators. How many are there, who sits where in the org, and how confident are you that the list is accurate, current, and reviewed by someone outside the backup team?

granular_questions.question: Are backup admin roles segregated from other infrastructure roles?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how segregation between backup admins, infrastructure admins, security admins, and application owners actually works in practice. Where are roles cleanly separated, and where does the same person quietly hold more than one hat?

granular_questions.question: How is backup admin access granted and revoked?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what happens when a new joiner needs backup admin access, or a leaver loses it. How quickly does it actually happen, what triggers the change, and where do gaps creep in between policy and execution?

granular_questions.question: Are privileged actions on backups logged and monitored?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how privileged actions on the backup platform (deletions, retention changes, policy modifications, immutability bypass) are logged, alerted on, and reviewed. Who watches the alerts, and what is the longest a suspicious action could plausibly go unnoticed?

granular_questions.question: Are there controls preventing unauthorized deletion of backups?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the controls preventing someone with admin access from deleting or shrinking backups. Immutability, retention locks, dual control, four-eyes? How would you know if any of those were quietly bypassed, and how recently has it been tested?

granular_questions.question: Are periodic access reviews conducted for backup admins?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how access reviews actually run. Are they real reviews where access gets removed, or attestation exercises where everyone clicks approve? When was the last time a review actually removed someone's privileges?

granular_questions.question: Are shared admin accounts used for backup systems?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us honestly where shared accounts still exist in the backup environment: vendor support, legacy tooling, scripts, scheduled jobs. Why are they still there, and what is the realistic plan to retire them?

granular_questions.question: Which backup administrative functions present the highest risk if misused?
granular_questions.discussion: Looking at the backup platform's full set of admin functions, which one would do the most damage in the wrong hands, and where today are the controls around it weakest? If you had to harden one thing this quarter, what would it be?

granular_questions.question: Are there any emergency admin paths that bypass standard segregation controls?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe any break-glass or emergency admin paths into the backup platform. Who knows about them, where are the credentials kept, and how confident are you that they would not be misused or, equally, that they would actually work in a crisis?

granular_questions.question: Is there separation of duty between backup administration and approval to restore production or sensitive data, or do backup admins effectively act as both gatekeepers and operators?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how decisions to restore production or sensitive data are separated from the people who actually perform the restore. Is there approval from a data owner before action, or do backup admins effectively act as both gatekeepers and operators?

granular_questions.question: Are admin actions on immutable copies, air-gapped vaults, or cyber recovery storage subject to additional controls such as dual approval, time-locks, or stepped-up authentication?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us what additional controls sit on top of immutable copies, air-gapped vaults, or cyber recovery storage. Time-locks, dual approval, separate credentials, stepped-up MFA on destructive actions? Where would a determined insider find the easiest path through?

granular_questions.question: How is backup admin access maintained if core identity services are unavailable?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how backup admins log in and operate when core identity services are unavailable. Is there a documented out-of-band path, has it been tested under realistic conditions, and who is authorised to invoke it?

granular_questions.question: How are privileged backup changes linked to change control and incident management?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how privileged backup changes flow through change management and into incident records. Where do urgent changes bypass that paper trail, and what is the audit posture if a regulator asks to reconstruct who did what during an incident?

granular_questions.question: Are vendor and third-party support paths into the backup platform inventoried, governed, and monitored (including session recording and just-in-time access)?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how vendor and third-party access into the backup environment is governed. Inventory of accounts, session recording, just-in-time elevation, named individuals? How do you know that when a support engineer logs in tonight, only what is authorised actually happens?

granular_questions.question: Does the backup platform depend on Active Directory for authentication?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what actually happens, technically and operationally, when a backup admin tries to log in or run a job and AD is sluggish or unresponsive. How much visibility do you have into how often that already happens during routine outages or maintenance?

granular_questions.question: Are backup service accounts dependent on AD?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through how backup service accounts are managed. Are they tied to AD, vaulted, rotating, MFA-protected? What is the worst case if those accounts get caught in the same incident that takes out the rest of identity?

granular_questions.question: Are dependencies between backup systems and identity infrastructure documented?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe where the dependency map between backup, identity, DNS, certificates, and storage actually lives. Is it documented and current, sitting in someone's head, or genuinely unknown? When did anyone last walk through it as a group?

granular_questions.question: What happens to backup operations if AD is unavailable?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the scenarios you have genuinely thought through. If AD goes down hard, say from ransomware on domain controllers, how long can backup operations limp along, what stops first, and at what point does recovery itself become impossible?

granular_questions.question: Are there alternative authentication mechanisms for backup access?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what alternate authentication looks like on your backup platforms today. Local break-glass accounts, MFA tokens, a separate identity provider, hardware keys? How recently has any of it been used in anger, and who knows where the credentials live?

granular_questions.question: Are there resilience measures for identity dependencies in backup systems?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the resilience measures you have in place today: a second AD forest, isolated identity for recovery, anything cloud-hosted. What is genuinely working, and what feels more like a paper control than a real one?

granular_questions.question: What non-AD dependencies could also prevent backup restore operations (DNS, network, storage, certificates, cloud services)?
granular_questions.discussion: Beyond AD, what other dependencies have you seen quietly block recovery in tests or incidents? DNS, KMS, certificates, license servers, cloud APIs, backup catalogues? Which of these worries you the most, and why?

granular_questions.question: Which backup workflows can continue during identity impairment, and which cannot?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through which backup workflows you genuinely believe can continue during a partial identity outage and which cannot. Where are you confident, and where is that confidence based on assumption rather than test evidence?

granular_questions.question: How are alternative authentication paths tested to ensure they are usable during a real event?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how alternate authentication paths get tested. Tabletop only, actual login under simulated outage, or never? What did you learn the last time you exercised it for real, and what changed afterwards?

granular_questions.question: What is the documented recovery order between backup platforms and identity services?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the documented recovery order between backup platforms and identity services. Who restores first, who waits, and how is that sequencing handled if both are damaged at the same time? Has it been rehearsed end-to-end?

granular_questions.question: How are backup encryption keys, certificates, and any KMS or HSM dependencies protected if the identity infrastructure they rely on is itself impaired?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how backup encryption keys, certificates, and any KMS or HSM the backup platform leans on are protected. If those are caught in the same blast radius as identity, what is the realistic plan to access keys without a working identity stack?

granular_questions.question: Has a tier-zero recovery scenario, where Active Directory itself must be restored before backups can be used, been planned, tabletopped, and rehearsed end-to-end?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what a true tier-zero rebuild looks like at GIC, where AD itself has to be restored before anything else can come back. How recently has that scenario been planned, tabletopped, or actually exercised end-to-end?

granular_questions.question: What backup platforms are currently deployed across the environment?
What backup throughput metrics are monitored?
How is restore performance measured and validated?
How is backup storage capacity tracked across tiers and repositories?
Are backup windows sufficient to complete jobs within required timeframes?
Are there known performance bottlenecks affecting backup or restore operations?
How are capacity thresholds defined and monitored for backup storage?
Is there a formal capacity planning process for backup infrastructure?
Are future growth and data expansion considered in backup capacity planning?
Do backup platforms meet RTO/RPO-driven performance expectations?
Are standard configuration baselines defined for backup platforms?
How are backup jobs defined and managed across systems?
Are retention policies defined and consistently applied?
Are backup configurations reviewed against vendor or industry best practices?
Is line-by-line configuration analysis performed for critical backup systems?
How are backup configuration changes approved and documented?
How is configuration drift detected in backup environments?
Are failed or missed backup jobs tracked and remediated?
Are backup configurations and policies audited regularly?
Are audit findings tracked through remediation?
What backup platforms and components are currently deployed in production?
What is the hardware lifecycle status of backup infrastructure?
What is the software lifecycle status of backup platforms and versions?
Are any backup systems running end-of-life or end-of-support versions?
What risks are associated with unsupported backup platforms?
What licensing models are used for backup solutions?
Are licenses sufficient for current capacity, features, and workloads?
Are there upcoming license renewals or expirations?
How is license compliance monitored and reported?
Are there cost optimisation opportunities in backup licensing?
Description
•Review the mechanisms used to protect backup data from modification or deletion, including immutability controls and logical or physical air-gapping approaches.
•Assess how backup platforms enforce tamper-resistant storage of backup copies to reduce exposure to ransomware attacks.
•Evaluate whether the backup architecture supports maintaining protected recovery copies even during a security incident.
•Review the organisation’s Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) definitions for critical systems and data.
•Assess how recovery objectives are aligned with the backup architecture and recovery mechanisms implemented across the environment.
•Evaluate whether recovery testing practices demonstrate that defined recovery objectives can realistically be achieved.

•Assess whether restore testing provides confidence that systems and data can be recovered within defined recovery objectives.
•Evaluate whether recovery validation practices provide a realistic view of operational recovery capabilities during disruption events.
•Review how database platforms are protected through backup mechanisms, including support for point-in-time recovery capabilities.
•Assess how database backup strategies integrate with the broader enterprise backup architecture.
•Evaluate whether database recovery approaches support restoration of critical data to known good states following operational or security incidents.
•Review how administrative access to backup platforms is controlled and segregated from other infrastructure roles.
•Assess whether backup administrative privileges are appropriately restricted and governed.
•Evaluate whether access controls help prevent unauthorised modification or deletion of backup data.
•Review dependencies between backup platforms and Active Directory or identity infrastructure, including authentication relationships and service dependencies.
