storage.label: Storage Resilience
storage.title: Storage Resilience & Recovery
storage.facilitator_intro: Start with the storage estate and what protects it before testing whether snapshots, replication, and encryption controls survive contact with a real cyber-recovery scenario. Use the sub-questions to push past polished answers and surface what has been operationally proven versus what is documented in policy.

layers.title: Architecture, Integrity & Protection Foundation
layers.intent: Establish what storage platforms exist, where crown-jewel data is actually written, and what controls keep that data intact and recoverable before probing isolation and access.

questions.primary: Paint a picture of the storage estate — what block, file, object, on-prem and cloud platforms protect which workload classes today, and where are the crown-jewel datasets actually written?
sub_questions: Which platforms protect which workload class — block, file, object, on-prem, cloud, hybrid?
Where are the crown-jewel datasets actually written, and which array or service hosts each?
Are there shadow storage systems — DAS, departmental NAS, unmanaged object stores — outside enterprise visibility?
What fraction of in-scope storage capacity is reporting health green today, and what is unmonitored?
Which workloads are explicitly out of scope of enterprise storage policy, and on what rationale?

questions.primary: What controls prevent and detect data corruption across storage platforms — array checksums, end-to-end protection, replication consistency — and how would silent bit-rot or storage-side corruption be discovered before recovery time?
sub_questions: What corruption-detection mechanisms run continuously — array checksum, T10-PI, scrubbing — and on which platforms?
How is replication consistency verified, and would a bit-flip propagating through replication be caught before or after recovery?
When was the last documented case of silent corruption on a production array, and how was it detected?
Are integrity scans periodic, on-demand, or triggered only at restore time?
For long-retention snapshots and immutable copies, how would year-old bit-rot be discovered before someone tries to recover from it?

questions.primary: What snapshot strategy underpins storage-layer protection — frequency, retention, immutability — and how confident are you that snapshots themselves are not at risk from the same threats they are meant to mitigate?
sub_questions: What is the snapshot frequency, retention, and immutability posture per tier — primary, secondary, vault?
Who owns snapshot policy — storage team, application owners, central protection function, or no one cleanly?
Where are snapshots load-bearing for recovery, and where are they decorative because backups will be used anyway?
Can a storage admin destroy or shorten snapshot retention unilaterally?
If ransomware ran against the array today, would the snapshot copies survive — and on what control basis?

layers.title: Replication, Isolation & Encryption Governance
layers.intent: Move from 'what is captured' to 'how is it isolated and protected' — this is where DR design intent and operational reality commonly diverge.

questions.primary: How is data replicated for resilience — synchronous, asynchronous, multi-site, vendor-native versus host-based — and what is the RPO each replication path actually delivers in production rather than on the design slide?
sub_questions: Which workloads replicate synchronous, async, or batch, and what is the actual measured RPO per path?
Is replication array-to-array, host-based, or vendor cyber-recovery (e.g. CyberSense, SnapMirror, SnapLock)?
Where are replication paths genuinely multi-site, and where is the DR copy sitting on the same fabric as production?
How is replication health monitored, and what is the MTTD on a replication path going silent?
Has a planned failover to the replicated copy been performed end-to-end in the last 12 months?

questions.primary: Is the replicated copy genuinely isolated from production identity, network, and admin plane — or does a compromised production storage admin reach the DR copy through the same blast radius?
sub_questions: Does the DR storage estate share identity with production — if production AD is encrypted, can DR storage be administered?
Is the management plane of replicated arrays reachable from the same admin network as production?
Are replication credentials and array service accounts held in production-side vaults that would be unavailable post-compromise?
Could a single compromised storage admin destroy production AND the replicated copy within the same session?
Where is the 'last known good' storage replica actually isolated, and who by name has the authority to invoke it?

questions.primary: What encryption is enforced at-rest across storage tiers, and where do the keys live — array-resident, external KMS, HSM, customer-managed — and what is the dependency posture between production identity and key access?
sub_questions: Which storage platforms enforce data-at-rest encryption today, and where is encryption configured but not enabled?
For each platform, where does the data-encryption key actually reside — array, external KMS, HSM, cloud KMS?
Are customer-managed keys (CMK) used where the platform supports them, or are vendor-managed defaults relied on?
Is encryption enforced consistently across primary, replicated, snapshot, and archival copies, or does archive silently drop encryption?
If production identity is unavailable, can storage admins still unlock encrypted volumes for recovery?

questions.primary: How are encryption keys rotated, escrowed, and recovered — and what happens to old immutable copies and long-retention snapshots when keys rotate or custodians turn over?
sub_questions: What is the documented key rotation cadence, and when was each platform's keys last rotated?
How does key rotation interact with snapshots and immutable copies — are old copies re-keyed, retained under old key, or invalidated?
Where are escrow / recovery copies of keys held, and who controls escrow access?
Has a 'no KMS, no identity, recover anyway' path ever been walked through end-to-end for storage?
What happens to long-retention immutable copies if their original key custodian leaves the firm?

layers.title: Access Controls, Detection & Integrity Validation
layers.intent: Probe who can touch storage administration, whether destructive actions can be performed unilaterally, and whether tampering would be seen in time to matter.

questions.primary: Who can administer storage arrays today — is admin identity separated from production, is MFA enforced, and is privileged access brokered through PAM, or are admins logging in with cached credentials?
sub_questions: Is storage admin identity in the same forest or Entra tenant as production users, or genuinely separated?
Is MFA enforced for every storage console, array management plane, and out-of-band controller?
Are storage admin sessions brokered through PAM, or do admins log in directly with cached credentials?
How are vendor support accounts (NetApp, Dell, Pure, HPE, IBM) granted access — time-bound, per-session approved, fully logged?
If the PAM platform itself is unavailable during a recovery scenario, how do storage admins authenticate?

questions.primary: What controls prevent unauthorized modification or deletion of storage objects, snapshots, LUNs and shares — and where does the line between 'soft-delete recoverable' and 'permanently destroyed' actually sit per platform?
sub_questions: What soft-delete or grace-period windows exist before snapshot delete, LUN destroy, or share removal becomes permanent?
Are destructive admin actions (snapshot delete, retention shorten, replication suspend, encryption disable) gated by dual-control or quorum?
Are storage admin actions session-recorded and reviewed for high-risk operations?
Can a single privileged admin destroy enough recovery surface in one session to break a tier-1 recovery objective?
Where does the line between 'recoverable mistake' and 'permanently destroyed' actually sit per platform?

questions.primary: What dual-control, quorum, or cooling-off enforcement exists for destructive storage actions — and would a single compromised admin be enough to dismantle the recovery posture?
sub_questions: Walk us through the approval flow if someone wanted to shorten a snapshot retention lock today — who signs, who approves?
Is dual-authorization or 4-eyes enforced for storage destructive actions, or documented but not technically enforced?
Are retention or lock changes logged immutably, and who actively reviews those logs?
Is there a cooling-off delay between request and execution for destructive operations, or do they execute immediately on approval?
What happens to delete requests during a declared incident — automatically frozen, or processed on the normal path?

questions.primary: How are storage and array logs forwarded, monitored and alerted on — and what specific scenarios trigger SOC action, and how fast?
sub_questions: Where are storage array logs forwarded — enterprise SIEM, isolated cyber-recovery SOC, or only locally retained?
What specific SIEM alerts fire for mass snapshot delete, retention change, replication suspension, encryption disable?
What is the documented MTTD for malicious storage tampering, and has it been measured rather than modelled?
Are storage admin actions correlated with identity-side anomalies (privileged logons, new accounts, AD changes)?
Are canary LUNs, honeypot shares, or decoy snapshots deployed to detect intruder reconnaissance on storage?

layers.title: Recovery Readiness & Dependencies
layers.intent: Test whether snapshots, replicas, and storage-side recovery can actually deliver under pressure, including database-resident data and the dependencies a responder would need to be alive first.

questions.primary: Have crown-jewel datasets been recovered end-to-end from storage replicas or snapshots in the last 12 months — under what scenarios, and what failed?
sub_questions: Of recovery tests in the last 12 months, how many specifically sourced data from storage snapshots or replicas rather than backup tier?
What is the documented recovery sequence when storage is the source of truth — DNS, identity, KMS, fabric — what must come first?
Have recovery tests included end-to-end snapshot-restore validation, or stopped at 'snapshot mounted'?
Are scenario-based tests run against storage (ransomware, regional loss, supply chain), or only technical-only failover drills?
Has a full end-to-end recovery from the DR-side storage replica been completed in the last 12 months?

questions.primary: How are database-resident datasets protected — application-consistent snapshots, log-shipping, native vendor backup — and are recovery procedures aligned across DBA, storage and infra teams, or do they diverge under pressure?
sub_questions: For each crown-jewel database (Oracle, MSSQL, Postgres, Mongo, Hadoop), what is the protection model — snapshot, native backup, log shipping, replication?
Are storage snapshots of databases application-consistent (quiesced, snapshot-aware), or crash-consistent?
Are DBA-side recovery procedures aligned with storage-side recovery procedures, or do they diverge under pressure?
When did the DBA, storage and infrastructure teams last run a joint database recovery test?
Where would database recovery hit the wall first — log replay, identity, schema mismatch, capacity?

questions.primary: What dependencies — identity, KMS, vCenter, hypervisor, network, fabric — must be alive before storage recovery can even begin, and have those dependencies themselves been recovery-tested or only assumed?
sub_questions: If production identity, DNS, and network are all unavailable, can storage admins still log in to initiate recovery?
Where is storage management metadata, snapshot catalogs, and replication state stored, and what is its own recovery posture?
Have storage dependencies (fabric, vCenter, hypervisor management, monitoring, ticketing) themselves been recovery-tested?
What is the documented rebuild plan for the storage management plane if it is compromised?
Has a 'cold start' — every dependency down, storage recovers from scratch — ever been walked through?

layers.title: Evidence & Priorities
layers.intent: Anchor the conversation in what has actually been proven on the storage side and where the highest-impact improvements lie.

questions.primary: If a cyber-compromise hit today and crown-jewel recovery depended on storage-resident snapshots or replicas, what would most likely undermine that recovery — and what single storage-domain improvement would most materially strengthen cyber recovery readiness?
sub_questions: Show us the most recent successful cyber-recovery test report that used storage as the recovery source — scenario, scope, outcomes?
What scenarios have been run against immutable snapshots or replicated copies in the last 12 months, and what failed?
If you had to name a single storage dependency that would break recovery today, what would it be — and why hasn't it been fixed?
Where would Day 2 of a real ransomware recovery hit the wall on the storage side — capacity, fabric, identity, snapshot integrity, scanning?
If you had budget and political capital for exactly one storage-domain improvement this year, what would deliver the most cyber-recovery uplift?
What does the 12-month storage-domain cyber-recovery roadmap actually look like, and how was it prioritised?

granular_questions.question: What controls are in place to prevent data corruption across storage platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the layers that prevent corruption today: array checksums, end-to-end protection information, replication consistency, snapshot integrity. Where do you trust the controls, and where would you not bet on them under a real corruption event?

granular_questions.question: How is unauthorized modification of stored data prevented or detected?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how unauthorized writes or modifications would actually be spotted. Real-time alerting, periodic scans, audit log review, or after-the-fact discovery during recovery? What is the realistic mean time to detect for an insider quietly altering data?

granular_questions.question: What safeguards exist to prevent accidental deletion of data?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the gap between someone clicking the wrong delete and that deletion becoming permanent. Grace periods, soft delete, snapshot fallbacks, retention locks. Where do these safeguards thin out across platforms?

granular_questions.question: Are snapshots used for data protection, and how are they managed?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through your snapshot strategy: frequency, retention, immutability, and who owns the policies. Where are snapshots load-bearing for recovery, and where are they treated as a nice-to-have backstop?

granular_questions.question: What access controls are applied at the storage layer?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how access at the storage layer differs from access at the OS or application layer. Are LUN, share, and array-management permissions all coherent, or does each platform have its own quirks that nobody fully tracks?

granular_questions.question: Are there different protection levels for critical vs non-critical data?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how protection levels are differentiated for critical versus non-critical data. Is the differentiation real (tier-1 immutable snapshots, tier-3 best-effort) or aspirational? Where has the line blurred over time?

granular_questions.question: How does the architecture protect enterprise and crown-jewel datasets?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the architecture protecting your crown-jewel datasets. Multiple platforms, isolated copies, diverse media, air gap. Where are you confident in the separation, and where are you worried that two copies could die together?

granular_questions.question: How is data integrity monitored and validated?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what data integrity monitoring actually looks like day to day. Who reads the scrub reports, how would a slowly degrading volume be caught early, and when did monitoring last surface a real problem before users did?

granular_questions.question: How are ransomware or suspicious encryption patterns detected at the storage layer?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what ransomware looks like at the storage layer and what would actually catch it early. Anomalous write patterns, entropy analysis, snapshot growth alerts, vendor analytics. How quickly would those alerts reach someone who could act?

granular_questions.question: What are the most likely failure modes for data corruption or data unavailability?
granular_questions.discussion: If you had to list the three most likely paths to corruption or data unavailability at GIC, what would they be? Hardware silently degrading, replication poisoning, admin error, code defect, ransomware. Where are mitigations weakest?

granular_questions.question: Which storage controls are most critical for protecting crown-jewel datasets during a disruptive event?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through which storage controls would actually matter most if a disruptive event hit tomorrow. What would you switch on, lock down, or pull as a known good copy first, and what is rehearsed versus theoretical?

granular_questions.question: How is integrity of recovered data validated before business use resumes?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how integrity of recovered data is validated before business sign-off. Hashes, application checks, business reconciliation, sample reviews. Who has authority to declare the data fit for use, and where does pressure to resume cut that step short?

granular_questions.question: How is silent data corruption (bit rot, latent sector errors, firmware defects) detected and remediated across the storage estate?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how silent data corruption gets caught at GIC. Where are you running active scrubs, where are you trusting vendor self-healing, and where is data quietly sitting on aging hardware that nobody is actively checking?

granular_questions.question: Who has administrative access to storage platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through who actually holds storage admin rights today across each major platform. Is the list current, reviewed by someone outside the storage team, and does it match what the platforms themselves say?

granular_questions.question: Are storage admin roles separated from other infrastructure roles?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how separation between storage, compute, network, security, and application admins works in practice. Where does it break down: vendor support, on-call rotations, after-hours incident response?

granular_questions.question: How is privileged access to storage systems granted and revoked?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how privileged storage access actually gets granted. Just-in-time, ticket-driven, role-based, or a mix? Where are people quietly carrying standing privileges they no longer need?

granular_questions.question: Are there controls restricting admin access scope?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how scope restriction is enforced inside platforms. Can a storage admin who manages tier-2 also touch tier-1, or are there hard fences? Where are those fences technical versus procedural?

granular_questions.question: Are shared or generic admin accounts used?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us honestly where shared or generic admin accounts persist: vendor support, scripts, automation, legacy tooling. Why are they still there, and what is the realistic path to retire them?

granular_questions.question: How is risk of privileged misuse mitigated?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the controls that genuinely sit between a privileged user and a destructive action. Approvals, dual control, session recording, stepped-up MFA, time-of-day restrictions. Where would a determined insider find the path of least resistance?

granular_questions.question: Which storage admin capabilities would have the greatest impact if abused or unavailable?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us which storage admin capabilities would do the most damage if abused: deletion, replication breakage, encryption key purge, snapshot policy modification. Where are the controls strongest, and where are they thinnest?

granular_questions.question: Are any storage administrative paths dependent on shared credentials or legacy controls?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the administrative paths that still lean on shared credentials, legacy consoles, or workarounds. How did they end up there, and what is keeping them in place?

granular_questions.question: Are admin activities logged and monitored?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what privileged action logging looks like, where the logs land, and who actually reviews them. What is the realistic time-to-detect for a quietly destructive action by someone with legitimate credentials?

granular_questions.question: Are there periodic reviews of storage admin access?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how access reviews actually work. Recertifications where access gets removed when needed, or attestation exercises where everyone clicks approve? When did one last lead to a real revocation?

granular_questions.question: How are privileged storage changes linked to change control and recovery governance?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how privileged storage changes flow through change management and into incident records. Where do urgent or out-of-cycle changes bypass the paper trail, and what would the audit position be if a regulator asked to reconstruct activity from a recent incident?

granular_questions.question: Is there separation of duty between storage administration and the approval of restore or destructive actions on production data?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how decisions to restore, overwrite, or destroy production data are separated from the people who actually perform those actions. Where do storage admins effectively act as both gatekeeper and operator, and where does that worry you most?

granular_questions.question: How would storage administration continue if primary identity services were unavailable?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how storage administration would actually function if AD or your primary identity provider went down. Is there a tested out-of-band path, who has the credentials, and how confident are you that it would hold up in a crisis?

granular_questions.question: What replication mechanisms are used between primary and DR sites?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the replication mechanisms in use across platforms today: array-based, host-based, hypervisor-level, application-native. Where is the choice deliberate, and where is it a legacy of platform sprawl?

granular_questions.question: Is replication synchronous or asynchronous?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us where synchronous replication is genuinely justified by business need versus inherited convention. Where has async drift bitten you in tests or incidents, and how are the trade-offs explained to business owners?

granular_questions.question: How frequently is data replicated?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how replication frequency is set, monitored, and adjusted. Where does it match the RPO commitment to the business, and where is there silent drift between contract and capability?

granular_questions.question: What storage platforms support DR replication?
granular_questions.discussion: Take us through which platforms have proper DR replication today, which have improvised paths, and which are quietly outside the DR perimeter. How was that current state arrived at, and is anyone actively closing the gaps?

granular_questions.question: Are failover and failback procedures documented?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what failover and failback procedures actually look like. Are they runbooks people could execute under pressure, or knowledge held in a few heads? When were they last updated based on a real test?

granular_questions.question: What are the RPO/RTO targets for storage recovery?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the gap between the storage-tier RPO/RTO documented in policy and what you would actually deliver under real pressure. Where is the storage commitment ahead of, or behind, what the application above it needs?

granular_questions.question: Does replication align with business continuity requirements?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how replication design ties back to BIA outputs and tiering. Where is the alignment current and revisited regularly, and where has the business changed without the storage architecture catching up?

granular_questions.question: Have DR storage scenarios been tested?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what real DR storage testing involves at GIC. How realistic are the scenarios, do tests include unplanned conditions, and how often does a test reveal something you genuinely did not expect?

granular_questions.question: Is replicated data validated for integrity at the destination, and how would replicated ransomware or corruption be detected and contained before failover?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how you would actually know whether the data at the DR site is clean. If ransomware or corruption replicated cleanly to DR, what would catch it before you cut over, and how confident are you in those controls today?

granular_questions.question: How are replication failures detected, triaged, and remediated?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how replication failures get spotted today. Who sees the alerts first, how often are alerts genuinely actioned versus snoozed, and when did a replication issue last get caught only by a test or an audit?

granular_questions.question: What happens to business services if replication is delayed but not fully failed?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the grey zone where replication is degraded but not stopped. How is that state handled operationally, who owns the call to invoke DR, and where has hesitation in that decision cost you in past incidents?

granular_questions.question: What dependencies must be available before storage failover/failback can succeed?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the dependencies that have to line up before a storage failover would actually work: identity, DNS, network, KMS, monitoring, runbooks, named operators on call. When was that chain last walked through end-to-end?

granular_questions.question: Are storage failover tests validated at the application level as well as the platform level?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how application teams are pulled into storage failover tests. Do they validate transactions, reconcile data, prove user access, or does the test stop at the storage service coming up at the DR site?

granular_questions.question: Is data-at-rest encryption enabled across storage platforms?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through where encryption-at-rest is genuinely on, where it is partially enabled, and where it is still on the to-do list. Are the gaps known to risk and audit, or quietly accepted?

granular_questions.question: What encryption standards and algorithms are used?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the diversity of encryption standards across the estate. Where do you have AES-256 with strong KMS integration, where are you reliant on vendor-default key handling, and where would crypto agility be a problem if a standard suddenly fell out of favour?

granular_questions.question: Are all storage tiers encrypted or only specific ones?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us where encryption coverage stops. Are backup tiers, DR copies, dev/test environments, and snapshot stores all encrypted to the same standard as production primary, or are there pockets of unencrypted data nobody talks about?

granular_questions.question: How is encryption enforced for sensitive or regulated data?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how encryption requirements driven by MAS, PDPA, or internal policy actually translate into platform configuration. Where is enforcement automated, and where does it rely on human discipline?

granular_questions.question: How are encryption keys themselves backed up, rotated, and recoverable, including offline or air-gapped key escrow for catastrophic scenarios?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how the keys themselves are protected. Backups, rotation cadence, offline escrow, geographic separation. If both production and DR KMS were lost in the same event, what is the realistic plan, and has it been rehearsed?

granular_questions.question: How are encryption keys managed and stored?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how keys live today across self-managed, vendor-managed, HSM-backed, and cloud KMS scenarios. Where is the key custody model clear, and where is it surprisingly fragile if a key were lost?

granular_questions.question: Is there integration with centralized key management systems?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how the centralized KMS plays with each storage platform. Where is integration deep and tested, and where is it superficial or one outage away from breaking?

granular_questions.question: Are there any exceptions to encryption policies?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the live exceptions today: legacy systems, performance constraints, vendor limitations. How are they documented, time-bound, reviewed, and how confident are you that the exception list is the actual list?

granular_questions.question: How is encryption compliance monitored?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how encryption compliance is monitored continuously rather than at audit time. What controls would catch a deliberately disabled encryption setting, and how quickly?

granular_questions.question: How are encryption exceptions reviewed from both security and resilience perspectives?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how exceptions are reviewed not just by security but by resilience. Where does an exception that satisfies security still create a recoverability problem, and who is responsible for spotting that?

granular_questions.question: What dependencies on KMS/HSM or centralized key services could affect storage recovery?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how a partial or full KMS outage would play out. Which platforms would keep operating, which would fail closed, and which would silently keep going while quietly accumulating risk?

granular_questions.question: Are key-management recovery procedures documented and tested?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through what KMS recovery testing has actually involved. Have you simulated KMS unavailability during recovery, or is the procedure a paper exercise? Who owns the keys-of-last-resort, and how recently has that path been used?

granular_questions.question: What business impact would result if encrypted storage could not be unlocked during recovery?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us honestly what happens if you cannot unlock encrypted storage during a real recovery. Which business services would stop, which clients would notice first, and how is that tail risk communicated upwards today?

granular_questions.question: How are critical datasets identified and classified?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how 'crown jewel' is genuinely defined at GIC and how that label translates into different storage and snapshot treatment. Where is the classification accurate and current, and where is it nominal?

granular_questions.question: What snapshot policies exist for critical data?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through the snapshot policies on tier-1 datasets: frequency, retention, immutability, off-array copies. Where are policies set deliberately, and where have they accreted over years?

granular_questions.question: How long are snapshots retained?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how snapshot retention has been set, by whom, and against what justification. Where does retention align with business and regulatory needs, and where is it tuned to capacity rather than risk?

granular_questions.question: How are snapshot policies aligned to application recovery sequencing and business criticality?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how snapshot policies map to application recovery order. Are tier-1 apps backed by snapshots aligned to their dependencies, or are snapshots set platform-by-platform without that lens?

granular_questions.question: Who can create, modify, or delete snapshots?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe the population that can create, modify, or delete snapshots today. Is that population tightly governed, broadly accessible, or somewhere in between, and how recently has the list been reviewed?

granular_questions.question: Are there controls preventing unauthorized snapshot deletion?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us what really prevents a malicious or careless snapshot deletion. Immutability flags, retention locks, dual approval, vendor-side restrictions. Where would a determined insider still find a way?

granular_questions.question: Are immutable or locked snapshots used?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through where immutable or locked snapshots are in use today. Are they covering the data that genuinely matters, and are the controls around lock duration, override, and authorisation strong enough to survive scrutiny?

granular_questions.question: How do snapshot controls protect against ransomware?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how snapshots would actually defend against ransomware. Immutability, isolation, vendor-side detection, off-array vaulting. Where is the protection real, and where is it marketing language?

granular_questions.question: Are snapshot activities logged and monitored?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how snapshot activity gets logged, where the logs go, and who actually watches them. What is the realistic time-to-detect for an unauthorised snapshot deletion or policy change?

granular_questions.question: What operational controls prevent snapshot sprawl, expiry, or misalignment with retention needs?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how snapshot sprawl is controlled at GIC. Who owns capacity, who reviews orphaned snapshots, and what happens when retention gets quietly cut to free space?

granular_questions.question: How is confidence established that a snapshot represents a clean, recoverable state?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how you would actually know a snapshot is clean. Application quiescing, integrity checks, post-snapshot validation, periodic test mounts. Where do you genuinely trust the snapshot, and where would you be checking once recovery started?

granular_questions.question: What dependencies are required to restore from snapshots during a crisis?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe what has to be present and working to restore from snapshots during a real crisis: identity, KMS, mount points, network, license servers, named operators on call. When did you last walk that chain end-to-end?

granular_questions.question: How are snapshots tested for restore at scale, and what is the realistic wall-clock time to mount, verify, and consume a snapshot for a tier-1 dataset?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how a tier-1 snapshot restore actually plays out under timing pressure. Mount time, verification, application reconnection, business validation. Where does the wall clock break in ways that the documented RTO does not capture?

granular_questions.question: What database-native encryption mechanisms are used?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through where database-native encryption is in use today (TDE, column-level, application-side) and where it overlaps or conflicts with storage-tier encryption. Where does that overlap give real defence-in-depth, and where is it just performance overhead?

granular_questions.question: How are database access controls enforced?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us how database-level access is governed and reconciled with the user identity at the OS, storage, and network layers. Where is access coherent end-to-end, and where do shadow accounts or service IDs make the picture murkier?

granular_questions.question: How is sensitive data within databases protected?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how sensitive data inside databases (PII, transactional, regulated) is identified, masked, tokenised, or encrypted. How do you know coverage is current as schemas evolve, and where has discovery been incomplete?

granular_questions.question: Are database backups protected and secured?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how database backups are protected end-to-end: encryption, access control, immutability, network exposure. Where is the protection at parity with production data, and where is the backup the soft target?

granular_questions.question: Are database audit logs enabled and monitored?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about database audit logging across platforms. Where is it on, where is it shipped to a SIEM, and where is it generated but never read? When did audit logging last detect an incident before something else did?

granular_questions.question: How are database-level permissions reviewed?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how DB permission reviews actually run. Real revocations, or attestation theatre? Where do legacy entitlements survive review cycles, and how long would it take to detect a quietly added privilege?

granular_questions.question: Are there controls separating DB admin and infrastructure roles?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through where DBAs, storage admins, and OS admins overlap. Where is separation enforced, where is it goodwill, and where would a single insider effectively control the data, the host, and the storage underneath?

granular_questions.question: How does database protection align with storage security policies?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us where database and storage security policies are actually consistent and where they diverge. Encryption standards, key handling, retention, immutability. Where does the database team accept storage-tier protection and vice versa, and where is there silent disagreement?

granular_questions.question: How would database protection controls function if storage replication or key management were impaired?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how database protection would behave if storage replication slowed, KMS became unavailable, or snapshot services failed. Where would databases keep running with degraded protection, and where would they fail closed?

granular_questions.question: How are corruption scenarios or partial data-loss conditions detected and handled?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how database corruption (logical, physical, partial) actually gets detected today. Block checksums, application errors, reconciliation failures, customer reports. Where do you trust detection, and where do you fear the slow burn?

granular_questions.question: What is the recovery path for the most critical databases if snapshot or storage-level recovery fails?
granular_questions.discussion: Tell us about the fallback recovery path for tier-1 databases when the snapshot or storage primary fails you. Native dumps, log shipping, replicated copies, cold backups. How recently has that fallback been exercised end-to-end?

granular_questions.question: How are database protection controls validated in real recovery testing?
granular_questions.discussion: Describe how database protection controls are tested under realistic recovery scenarios. Are encryption, audit, access, and integrity all proven post-restore, or does testing stop when the database starts? Where do you suspect a real recovery would expose gaps?

granular_questions.question: How are TDE or database-native encryption keys protected, escrowed, and recoverable independently of the storage-layer KMS?
granular_questions.discussion: Walk us through how TDE and native database encryption keys are protected and escrowed. If the storage KMS is unavailable or compromised, can databases still be unlocked, and how recently has that independence actually been validated?

service_mgmt.label: Service Management
service_mgmt.title: Service Management Resilience
service_mgmt.facilitator_intro: Start with the CMDB and crown-jewel service identification before testing whether dependency mapping, change governance, and incident response can actually support a cyber-recovery scenario rather than routine operations.

layers.title: CMDB & Service Catalogue Foundation
layers.intent: Establish what the CMDB contains, who owns it, and whether crown-jewel services are explicitly identified within it.

questions.primary: Paint a picture of the CMDB — what platform, what classes of CI are populated, who owns the data, and who actually consumes it?
sub_questions: Which CMDB platform is in use, and is there a single authoritative instance or multiple parallel sources?
Which CI classes are populated — applications, servers, databases, network, identity, business services?
Who owns CMDB data integrity, and how is that ownership operationally enforced?
Which downstream processes consume CMDB data — change, incident, problem, recovery — and which bypass it?
What percentage of CIs have an active owner attribute, and what fraction is orphaned?

questions.primary: How are crown-jewel and tier-1 services explicitly identified in the CMDB, and is that identification maintained or last touched years ago?
sub_questions: Is there a documented crown-jewel / tier-1 / MAS-critical attribute on services, and when was it last reviewed?
Who has authority to assign or change a service tier — IT, business, risk, or no one cleanly?
Are tier assignments aligned with BIA outputs and regulatory criticality (MAS TRM, CSA CCoP)?
How is tier inheritance handled — does a tier-1 service automatically tier its dependencies, or are they classified separately?
Show us the current tier-1 service list — would the business agree it is complete and accurate?

questions.primary: What is the discovery and freshness model — automated scanning, periodic attestation, or manual entry — and what fraction of CIs are stale beyond policy thresholds?
sub_questions: What discovery tooling populates the CMDB, and what is its coverage across the estate?
How often are CIs reconciled or re-attested, and by whom?
What is the documented staleness threshold, and what fraction of CIs are currently in breach?
Are shadow IT assets (departmental SaaS, unmanaged systems) flagged as outside CMDB coverage?
When was the last full reconciliation between CMDB and a ground-truth source (vCenter, AD, AWS Org)?

layers.title: Dependency Modelling & Service Impact
layers.intent: Move from 'what exists' to 'what depends on what' — dependency depth is where service-management maturity diverges from operational reality.

questions.primary: How are service-to-CI dependencies mapped today — top-down by service owner, bottom-up by discovery, or hybrid — and how deep does the mapping go?
sub_questions: What approach is used — manual mapping, automated topology discovery, observability-driven, or hybrid?
How deep does mapping go — application only, or down through middleware, database, storage, network, identity?
Are external dependencies (SaaS, third parties, payment networks, market data) captured?
Are dependencies versioned over time, or only kept current?
Who validates dependency accuracy, and how often?

questions.primary: What is the operational use of dependency data — does it inform change, incident, and recovery decisions, or is it referenced only during audits?
sub_questions: Does CAB use dependency data to assess change blast radius?
During an incident, is the dependency map consulted to triage impact, or is institutional knowledge relied on?
When was the last documented case of dependency data preventing a bad change or accelerating a recovery?
Do business service owners trust the dependency view enough to act on it in a crisis?
Is the dependency map referenced in cyber-recovery playbooks, or only in routine continuity docs?

questions.primary: For a named tier-1 business service, can you trace its dependency tree end-to-end (app → middleware → database → storage → network → identity), and how confident are you the trace is correct today?
sub_questions: Pick a tier-1 service today — can you produce its dependency tree from CMDB in under five minutes?
How many of those dependencies have current, verified ownership in the CMDB?
Have any of those dependencies changed in the last 30 days, and was the CMDB updated?
If a single CI in that tree is encrypted in a ransomware event, what is the immediate impact assessment process?
Where would the dependency trace fail — and how often does it fail in practice?

layers.title: Change, Incident & IR Governance
layers.intent: Test whether change and incident processes are coherent, integrated with security, and capable of operating under pressure.

questions.primary: What change governance model is in place, and how is risk specifically evaluated for changes touching crown-jewel services or recovery infrastructure?
sub_questions: What change categories exist (standard, normal, emergency), and how is each routed?
How is risk scored for a change, and who has veto authority for high-risk changes?
Are changes to backup, storage, identity, and recovery infrastructure flagged for elevated scrutiny?
What is the documented post-implementation review cadence, and who reads the output?
When was the last change-induced incident traceable to a CAB gap?

questions.primary: How are post-change outcomes managed — do failures feed back into the CAB, CMDB, and process improvements, or are they handled in isolation?
sub_questions: What fraction of changes are categorised as successful vs partial vs failed, and is the trend visible?
Where do change-failure root causes land — service management, security, or both?
Are recurring change-failure patterns surfaced and addressed structurally?
Does change failure data influence the assessed risk of future similar changes?
Are change outcomes correlated to incident records to identify change-induced outages?

questions.primary: Describe your incident response model — who owns severity, who declares major, and how does the IT-side IR intersect with security IR?
sub_questions: What is the severity taxonomy, and who has authority to escalate or de-escalate?
At what severity is security IR automatically engaged?
Are IT incident and security incident streams reconciled in real time, or only post-mortem?
What is the documented hand-off process when an IT incident is suspected to be a cyber event?
Who chairs the war room when the line between incident and breach is unclear?

questions.primary: How are incident, problem, and major-incident records integrated with the security operations stream and the threat intel pipeline?
sub_questions: Are incident tickets and SIEM cases correlated through a shared identifier or workflow?
Do post-incident reviews include security review, or only operational review?
Is threat-intel context attached to incident records when relevant?
When was the last incident reclassified as a cyber event mid-flight, and how did the model handle it?
Are root-cause findings shared between SOC and ITSM teams structurally, or only ad-hoc?

questions.primary: When was your last major outage, and walk us through how the execution model actually performed — comms, war room, business engagement, decision pace?

identity.label: Identity
identity.title: Identity Resilience & Recovery
identity.facilitator_intro: Identity is tier-zero — the question is not whether AD and Entra are present, but whether they survive contact with a determined attacker and whether crown-jewel services can be recovered when identity itself is impaired. Push past 'we have MFA' answers to what is operationally proven.

•Review how identity and access management controls apply to managed database services, including authentication and identity integration approaches.
•Assess the use of directory-based authentication, service identities, and access controls for database services where applicable.
•Evaluate how database access is governed within the broader enterprise identity model.
•Identity service resilience considerations, including domain controller recovery models, identity service failover mechanisms, and disaster recovery procedures.
•Processes and capabilities supporting identity service restoration or recovery following service disruption.
•Processes used to manage user identity lifecycle events, including onboarding, role changes, and employee departures.
•Controls governing identity provisioning, modification, and deprovisioning aligned with HR processes.

granular_questions.subdomain: Complete IAM rules, policies, and structure review, RBAC
granular_questions.question: •Detailed assessment of IAM policies, access rules, and role-based access control (RBAC) structures across enterprise systems.
•Design and effectiveness of access role models, policy frameworks, and entitlement structures.
•Platforms and tools used to manage and administer identity infrastructure, including IAM management platforms and identity governance tools.
•Capabilities of identity tooling used for identity lifecycle management, access provisioning, and access governance.

network.label: Network
network.title: Network Resilience & Segmentation
network.facilitator_intro: Start with what the network architecture actually looks like and where the trust boundaries sit, then push past polished segmentation diagrams to what enforcement is operationally proven and what would survive a real cyber-compromise.

layers.title: Data Centre & Network Architecture Baseline
layers.intent: Establish DC topology, redundancy posture, and documentation state before probing controls.

questions.primary: Paint a picture of the data centre and network topology — JDC, KDC, sites, inter-DC links, cloud on-ramps — and where the network actually carries crown-jewel traffic.
sub_questions: How many DCs, sites, and cloud regions carry production workloads?
What are the inter-DC link types, capacities, and providers?
Which workloads traverse public internet, MPLS, or dedicated cloud paths?
Are there test, dev, or vendor environments riding the same network?
Where does crown-jewel traffic concentrate, and are those paths explicitly mapped?

questions.primary: What is the availability design — redundancy at each layer, ECMP, multi-path routing — and what single points of failure remain despite the diagrams?
sub_questions: Where is redundancy genuine (active-active, ECMP) versus active-passive with manual failover?
Are uplinks, route reflectors, and gateways all redundant across both DCs?
Are layer-2 extension dependencies (VXLAN, OTV) understood as risk?
What network SPOFs are known and accepted today?
When was the last documented network-path SPOF discovery exercise?

questions.primary: What is the state of network documentation and recovery artefacts — diagrams, configs, vendor support data — and how confident are you it is current?
sub_questions: When were architecture diagrams last refreshed to match production?
Where do device configurations live, and how are they backed up and versioned?
Is golden-config baseline maintained, and is drift detected?
Are runbooks for major path failures current, owned, and tested?
Where does vendor support contact and serial-number data live?

layers.title: Segmentation & Control Points
layers.intent: Probe the segmentation design and where enforcement actually holds versus is documented but bypassable.

questions.primary: Describe the segmentation model — zones, VRFs, microsegmentation, software-defined — and how it maps to business risk and crown-jewel services.
sub_questions: What zone model is in use (PCI, prod, dev, OT, DMZ), and what enforces zone boundaries?
Is microsegmentation in place (Illumio, NSX, Cisco SD-Access), and what is its coverage?
Where do east-west flows cross zones without enforcement?
Are crown-jewel services in dedicated zones, or share with general workloads?
What process governs zone-boundary exceptions?

questions.primary: What enforcement points actually inspect east-west traffic — firewalls, microseg agents, fabric ACLs — and how are exceptions tracked?
sub_questions: Where are inter-zone flows inspected today?
What inspection happens within a zone, if any?
How are temporary exceptions (project, testing) governed and retired?
Are policy changes peer-reviewed and tested before push?
What is the documented review cadence for east-west rules?

questions.primary: How is segmentation effectiveness validated — purple-team, breach-and-attack simulation, real-world incident — and what has it revealed?
sub_questions: Has segmentation been tested with adversary emulation (Atomic Red Team, AttackIQ, SafeBreach)?
When was the last lateral-movement test, and which controls failed?
Are findings tracked to closure with measured re-test?
Are detection-side controls validated alongside enforcement?
What residual lateral-movement risk would you flag to leadership today?

layers.title: Perimeter, External Access & Resilience
layers.intent: Test perimeter design, third-party connectivity, and failover behaviour.

questions.primary: What is the perimeter and DMZ design — inbound zones, reverse proxies, WAF, DDoS — and where does the design fall short under pressure?
sub_questions: What sits at the edge — firewalls, WAF, DDoS, reverse proxies — and in what order?
Is the DMZ a real zone with inspection or a flat segment with port openings?
How are SSL/TLS inspection decisions made and governed?
What inbound services are exposed today, and is the inventory current?
When was the last edge configuration peer-reviewed?

questions.primary: How are third-party connectivity paths (MPLS, dedicated circuits, SaaS, partners, vendors) governed — and which are over-trusted relative to risk?
sub_questions: Inventory of third-party connections — circuits, IPSec, peering, SaaS integrations?
What controls sit between third-party endpoints and production?
How is third-party connectivity reviewed and retired when no longer needed?
Are vendor accesses time-bound and session-recorded where they touch admin planes?
What would happen if a major third party (SWIFT, market data, payment) became hostile or compromised?

questions.primary: What is the SPOF and failover model — links, devices, paths — and what is the validated RTO for each failure mode?
sub_questions: Where is failover automatic versus manual?
What is the measured failover time per major scenario?
When was each failover scenario last live-tested?
Are devices clustered, and what is the failure mode if cluster syncing fails?
Are LB and DNS failover scripts current and tested?

questions.primary: How are load balancers and DNS — both authoritative and resolver — protected and operated, and what is the cyber-recovery posture for those layers?
sub_questions: What LB platforms are in use, and are they redundant across DCs?
Where does authoritative DNS live, and what is the change-control posture?
How is DNSSEC handled, and how is cache-poisoning resistance measured?
If DNS is compromised, what is the documented containment path?
Are LB configurations versioned and recoverable?

layers.title: Recovery & Business-Service Continuity
layers.intent: Probe whether the network plane itself can be recovered and whether business-service mapping is real.

questions.primary: Can a tier-1 business service be traced end-to-end through the network — paths, zones, devices — and how confident are you the trace is current?
sub_questions: For a named tier-1 service, what is the network path from user to data?
Are paths documented per service or only per device?
What network change in the last 90 days could have invalidated the trace?
Who owns the trace and keeps it current?
How is the trace used during incident triage?

questions.primary: What is the recovery sequence for the network plane itself — management, control, data — if compromise reaches the network management stack?
sub_questions: Is the network management plane separated from production, with its own identity?
Where do device configs and credentials live during a network-management compromise?
What is the rebuild plan for the management plane?
Are out-of-band paths to devices defined and tested?
What dependencies (DNS, NTP, identity, monitoring) must be alive for network recovery to start?

questions.primary: How is the network management plane itself protected during cyber events — out-of-band, jump hosts, OOB credentials?
sub_questions: Is OOB connectivity to devices in place and tested?
Are admin jump hosts dedicated, hardened, and monitored?
Where are device credentials stored if the credential vault is unavailable?
Has a 'network management plane down' scenario been exercised?
Who has the authority to invoke OOB paths during an incident?

layers.title: Evidence & Priorities
layers.intent: Anchor in evidence and the single biggest network-domain uplift.

questions.primary: Show us the most recent segmentation, lateral-movement, or perimeter validation evidence — what was tested, what failed, what was fixed?
sub_questions: What red-team or purple-team activity has stressed the network in the last 12 months?
What east-west controls were proven, and which assumed?
Were findings tracked to closure with measured re-test?
Are auditors / regulators satisfied with current network posture?
What residual network risk would you raise to leadership today?

questions.primary: If you had budget and political capital for exactly one network improvement this year, what would most materially strengthen cyber-recovery readiness — and why hasn't it been done?
sub_questions: Name the single highest-impact network improvement, and the constraint blocking it.
Where does the 12-month network roadmap explicitly invest in recovery rather than capacity or refresh?
What would change if microsegmentation was truly enforced across crown-jewel services tomorrow?
What residual risk remains even after the best single improvement?
What is the smallest credible step that could change recovery posture in 90 days?

granular_questions.question: How are the two data centres (JDC, KDC) interconnected?

granular_questions.question: What DNS, DHCP, NTP, and load-balancing services are required for DC-to-DC recovery?

security_risk.label: Security & Risk
security_risk.title: Security Controls & Risk Posture
security_risk.facilitator_intro: Start with the perimeter and segmentation controls that constitute the primary security envelope, then push through PAM, EDR, SIEM, and ransomware-IR readiness to what is operationally proven rather than documented.

layers.title: Perimeter & Boundary Security Controls
layers.intent: Establish firewall and segmentation posture and the change-management discipline around them.

questions.primary: Paint a picture of the firewall estate — platforms, generations, where each one sits, and which crown-jewel flows it protects.
sub_questions: Which firewall platforms and generations are in production (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point, Cisco)?
Where does each firewall sit — perimeter, internal, DC, branch, cloud edge?
Which flows traverse multiple firewall layers, and which are inspected at only one point?
Are firewall licenses, capacity, and EOL status known and tracked?
Where do legacy or unmanaged firewalls still exist?

questions.primary: Describe the firewall policy model — rule structure, NAT, application identification, threat prevention — and how policy hygiene is maintained.
sub_questions: Is policy structured by zone, app, or legacy port-based?
What fraction of rules are using application-ID and identity-based criteria?
How many shadowed, overlapping, or any-any rules exist today?
When was the last rule-base cleanup, and what was the rule-count delta?
Is rule expiry / review enforced, or are rules eternal?

questions.primary: How is firewall change governance enforced — peer review, testing, drift detection, separation of duty?
sub_questions: Is firewall change peer-reviewed, and by whom?
Are emergency changes tracked and reconciled post-event?
How is config drift between intended and actual policy detected?
What separation-of-duty exists between policy author, approver, and pusher?
Are firewall change failures categorised and fed back into governance?

layers.title: Endpoint, Identity Access & PAM
layers.intent: Move from boundary to host-level and identity-level controls — PAM scope, EDR coverage, integration with the broader stack.

questions.primary: What is PAM coverage and lifecycle governance today — scope, account types, vault rotation, session brokerage?
sub_questions: Which platforms route through PAM (AD, network, storage, backup, cloud, SaaS, DB)?
Which privileged-account types are in PAM versus outside (vendor, service, break-glass)?
Are session recordings retained, and is high-risk-action review performed?
What credential-rotation cadence is enforced, and is it automated?
When was the PAM platform itself last security-reviewed?

questions.primary: What is the EDR / XDR platform, coverage, and operating model — and where does coverage end?
sub_questions: Which EDR platform is in use, and what is the deployed fleet coverage (% endpoints, % servers)?
Are unmanaged or legacy endpoints (OT, IoT, vendor) excluded — and why?
Is EDR data forwarded to SIEM or operated as a separate console?
Is EDR in detect, prevent, or block mode for each control class?
What is the alert-to-investigation pipeline, and who owns it?

questions.primary: How is EDR detection and prevention designed — out-of-the-box vs tuned, custom rules, identity correlation?
sub_questions: What custom detections have been authored beyond vendor defaults?
Are MITRE ATT&CK coverage and gaps measured?
Is EDR-identity correlation in place (suspicious logon + suspicious binary)?
Are EDR exclusions inventoried and reviewed?
How often is the detection rule-set tuned vs left static?

questions.primary: How does EDR integrate with the broader stack — SOAR, SIEM, identity, network — and what is the validated MTTR for an EDR-triggered case?
sub_questions: What automated actions are wired between EDR and SOAR (isolate, quarantine, reset)?
Is enrichment (identity, asset tier, recent change) automatic on case creation?
What is the measured MTTD and MTTR for high-fidelity EDR cases?
Are EDR cases reviewed for false-positive vs true-positive ratios?
How is EDR coverage and uptime monitored?

layers.title: Detection, Logging & Monitoring
layers.intent: Probe SIEM coverage, use-case maturity, and oversight to assess whether tampering or compromise would actually be seen in time.

questions.primary: What is the SIEM coverage and logging architecture — sources, retention, ingest health — and where are critical sources missing?
sub_questions: Which platform is in use, and what is the daily ingest volume?
Which log sources are required by policy but not connected today?
What is the retention model for hot vs cold logs?
How is ingest health monitored, and what is the alert if a source goes silent?
Are tier-0 sources (DC security log, KMS, PAM, backup admin) all on?

questions.primary: What is the use-case library maturity — MITRE coverage, custom analytics, tuning cadence — and where are detection gaps known to be?
sub_questions: How many production use-cases exist, and how are they mapped to ATT&CK?
What is the documented coverage gap, and where is it documented?
How often are use-cases tuned, retired, or added?
Are detections measured for false-positive rate, true-positive rate, time-to-detect?
Is detection engineering a defined team function or an ad-hoc activity?

questions.primary: What is the monitoring and oversight model — 24x7 SOC, MDR, hybrid — and where are blind spots in escalation or analyst tier coverage?
sub_questions: Is SOC in-house, MSSP, or hybrid, and what is each tier responsible for?
What is the documented escalation path during off-hours and major incidents?
Are analyst tier handoffs clean, and is context preserved?
Are MDR providers SLA-bound on response time and outcome?
When did SOC last surface a tier-1 incident in real time?

layers.title: Incident, Ransomware & Remote-Access Readiness
layers.intent: Test whether ransomware-IR and remote-access controls hold under real conditions.

questions.primary: Describe the ransomware IR playbook and ownership today — who owns it, how current is it, when was it last exercised?
sub_questions: Who is the named owner of the ransomware playbook, and when was it last updated?
Is the playbook scenario-specific (encryption, exfiltration, double-extortion) or generic?
Are roles defined down to the named individual or only by function?
When was the last tabletop or live exercise?
What changed structurally after the last exercise?

questions.primary: How is ransomware detection and escalation designed — what triggers a 'this is ransomware' declaration, and who has authority to do it?
sub_questions: What technical signals trigger ransomware suspicion (mass file change, EDR, honey-file)?
Who declares ransomware, and what timeline must they meet?
Are SOC, ITSM, identity, and storage teams simultaneously alerted?
What is the documented decision authority for shutting down critical systems?
When was the last suspected ransomware incident, and how did the declaration timeline behave?

questions.primary: What containment and isolation capability exists — network, identity, endpoint — and how fast can it be invoked?
sub_questions: Can the SOC isolate endpoints at scale via EDR — what is the measured time?
Can identity disable affected accounts or revoke tokens at scale?
Are network containment paths (BGP, ACL, NAC) ready and tested?
Can third-party connectivity be cut quickly?
What is the documented blast-radius containment objective?

questions.primary: How is recovery decisioning structured — who decides to pay versus rebuild, who validates clean state, who signs off on reintroduction?
sub_questions: Is there a pre-approved decision tree for ransom payment versus rebuild?
Who validates that a recovery candidate is clean before reintroduction?
What is the documented criteria for declaring a system clean?
Who has signing authority for each major recovery decision?
Has the legal / regulatory / insurance path been pre-walked?

questions.primary: What is the VPN, ZTNA, and internet-access posture for remote work and third-party access — and where does it remain a soft target?
sub_questions: What VPN / ZTNA platform is in use, and is it MFA-enforced end-to-end?
How is split-tunnel vs full-tunnel governed?
Are vendor / third-party VPN paths separated from employee paths?
How are exposure and patching of the VPN/ZTNA platform itself managed?
When was the last VPN posture review or red-team exercise?

layers.title: Framework Alignment & Priorities
layers.intent: Anchor in security framework posture and the single biggest improvement.

questions.primary: Which security frameworks anchor your control set today — NIST CSF, ISO 27001, MAS TRM, CSA CCoP, PCI-DSS — and where does framework coverage hide real gaps?
sub_questions: Which frameworks are formally adopted, and which are mapped but not adopted?
Where do frameworks overlap, and where do gaps fall between them?
What is the documented owner of framework conformance?
How is framework drift detected as controls change?
Are framework results communicated to leadership and the board?

questions.primary: What is the audit and certification posture — open findings, remediation track record, regulator-facing evidence — and where are findings repeatedly recurring?
sub_questions: What audit / certification activity is current (ISO, SOC 2, regulator, internal)?
How many findings are open, and how many are aged beyond SLA?
Which findings recur audit-over-audit, and why?
How is evidence collection automated versus manual?
When was the last regulator interaction, and what was their take?

questions.primary: If you had budget and political capital for exactly one security improvement this year, what would most materially strengthen cyber-recovery readiness — and why hasn't it been done?
sub_questions: Name the single highest-impact security improvement on the backlog.
What constraint blocks it — funding, ownership, vendor capability, risk appetite?
